articles.title: Why Is the Sky Blue?
paragraphs: Sunlight looks white, but it is actually a mix of many colors. When this light enters the air, it hits tiny gas molecules. These molecules {{scatter|scatter}} short blue waves much more than long red ones, sending blue light in every direction. That is why we {{perceive|perceive}} the sky as blue during the day.

At sunset, the light must travel through far more air before it reaches our eyes. Most of the blue light is scattered away long before it arrives, so the reds and oranges remain. The same physics explains why {{distant|distant}} mountains often look slightly blue. Scientists call this effect Rayleigh scattering, after the British physicist who described it in the 1870s.

articles.title: Where Did the Word 'Robot' Come From?
paragraphs: The word robot is younger than many people think. It first appeared in 1920 in a play by the Czech writer Karel Čapek. The play, called R.U.R., showed factory-made workers who did every task for humans. Čapek's brother Josef suggested the name. It came from the Czech word robota, which means forced labor.

In the story, the robots eventually {{rebel|rebel}} against the people who made them. The idea was so {{influential|influential}} that the word quickly spread to other languages. Today, robots build cars and explore Mars, but the word still {{carries|carry}} a trace of its old meaning: a machine made to work for someone else.

articles.title: An Animal with Three Hearts
paragraphs: An octopus has three hearts. Two of them pump blood through the gills, where it picks up oxygen. The third sends that blood to the rest of the body. Octopus blood is also blue, not red, because it uses a copper-based molecule to carry oxygen.

However, this system has a cost. When an octopus swims, the main heart {{temporarily|temporary}} stops beating, so swimming quickly tires it out. That may explain why octopuses often prefer to crawl along the sea floor. Their bodies show how animals {{adapt|adapt}} to their environment in {{remarkable|remarkable}} ways.
